svg.text: Stage 8 — the database says no (2026-11-10)
Row-level security turned on for every table, with no policies. ADR 026.
THE PUBLIC INTERNET → SUPABASE
Supabase's security advisor (2026-11-08) flagged every public-schema table as open: anyone holding the public anonymous key could read
profiles, e-mails, password hashes and the catalogue via the auto-generated REST API. The app never uses that API or that key.
What changed
Row-level security enabled on all 28
application tables, plus a sweep for any
other public table — and zero policies.
No policy = the anonymous and authenticated
roles see and write nothing. Grants revoked
on existing and future objects.
What did not change
The app connects as the table owner,
which RLS does not restrict. Every
query the app makes works exactly as before.
A regression test fails the suite if a new
table is added without RLS. Rehearsed against
a real PostgreSQL first: 28 open → 0.
Plain version: the front door to the data was never used, so it was bricked up. The app's own door still works.
Drawn from d316f99 · eac8f30 (verification query) · ADR 026 · specs/35-production-database-access-control.md · test: server/src/postgres-rls.test.ts
